Synopsis:
A short dialog for the flaming fist patroling inside of the Big Barn which holds donations for the refugees. Same dialog will be used in a case of this flaming fist catching the player inside the barn.

Cluster Contexts:
- WYR_RefugeeCamp_FlamingFist_003.json: The Big Barn is a restricted storage area holding donated supplies for refugees and is patrolled by Flaming Fist soldiers who treat theft or trespass as a serious offense. Broadhorn’s brusque “halt” is an enforcement call — off‑screen the player has been caught inside the barn rummaging or otherwise acting suspiciously. This fits the same tense looting/trespass pattern seen elsewhere: guards are primed to warn, demand explanations, and quickly escalate if the player lies, resists, or tries to bargain. The exchange can therefore lead to compliance and a warning, confiscation/arrest, or confrontation depending on the player’s response.
- WYR_RefugeeCamp_FlamingFist_001.json: Rowan is a Flaming Fist sentinel posted at the back door of the Big Barn, which is being used to store donated goods for refugees — a place the city takes seriously and guards closely. Off‑screen there’s reason for suspicion: recent looting, trespass, and tense small‑scale confrontations in the area mean guards are primed to challenge anyone near or inside the barn. Rowan’s curt demand for a one‑word reason signals official impatience and the expectation you’ll either have a simple, legitimate answer or face escalation (a warning, search, detainment, or combat if you’re caught trespassing). The same short exchange is used whether you’re stopped outside the door or discovered inside the barn.
- WYR_RefugeeCamp_FlamingFist_002.json: A short dialog for the flaming fist guarding the Big Barn next to his manip. The barn holds donations for the refugees. Same dialog will be used in a case of this flaming fist catching the player inside the barn.
- WYR_RefugeeCamp_FlamingFist_006.json: Fist Varone is a female Flaming Fist caster posted to guard the Big Barn — a locked storage of donated supplies for refugees — and she does the duty grudgingly but firmly. Her “Back again?” indicates the player has already been warned or caught here before, so she treats them as a repeat trespasser. Off‑screen there are enforcement rules and likely backup/alarm procedures for protecting the barn’s contents, so Varone threatens to take the player to the cells and will raise the alarm if resisted. This short exchange is the same whether the player is trying to enter or is caught inside, and available responses typically include surrender, fleeing, or fighting to prevent her from calling for reinforcements.
- WYR_RefugeeCamp_FlamingFist_005.json: A Flaming Fist soldier (Fist Madigan) is inside the Big Barn—a location treated as a restricted area—and, though he’s been lazing about, he enforces the law when he spots you. He calls out your trespass, orders you to come quietly so you can “mull over” your mistake in a jail cell, and warns that the conversation can continue en route. Off‑screen this implies the player has been in the barn unlawfully (hiding, snooping, or looting) and that nearby guards or witnesses could be alerted. The player can either submit to arrest or resist—refusal typically escalates to combat or other enforcement, consistent with the game’s standard trespass/loot confrontation scenes.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Fist Broadhorn: Halt, citizen! This is a restricted area - explain yourself. || [context] NodeContext: Stern and forceful; clearly loves her job (node 8)
- Player: I was looking to see if there was anything worth stealing. (node 16)

context: The Big Barn is a locked, restricted storage of donated supplies for refugees and is patrolled by Flaming Fist soldiers; the same short exchange is used whether a guard stops you at the door or catches you inside. Off‑screen the player has been discovered in the barn rummaging, looting, or otherwise acting suspiciously, which prompts a brusque “halt” and demand for a succinct explanation. Guards (Broadhorn, Rowan, Varone, Madigan are representative examples) are primed to warn, search, confiscate, detain, or raise an alarm and will escalate quickly if you lie, resist, or try to bargain. The encounter can therefore resolve with compliance and a warning/escort, confiscation and arrest, or a violent confrontation if the player fights or flees.
